Tesla’s New Roadster Is a Real Stuntcar, Do You Like It More in Red? (Rendering)
6 photos
Photo: Instagram | theottle
Everyone and their pet are talking about the all-new Tesla Roadster today, because it is the thing that pretty much broke the internet. You have likely seen it already, found out what it is capable of, on paper, anyway, and watched the videos that show it in action.
So, what is this story all about then? Well, it’s not only those who reshare the clips on social media that want a small chunk of the viral pie, as so does the rendering crowd. One of the first virtual takes on this model after the official unveiling can be seen in the photo gallery above, and embedded at the bottom of this story, and it came from @theottle on Instagram.
If you are familiar with this rendering artist’s work, then you know that he tends to keep things realistic. And he wasn’t going to pull a different stunt in this case, because the all-new Tesla Roadster has had its pixels rearranged in order to wear a new color. It’s glossy red, and it is joined by the usual black accents on the lower parts of the body. The wheels carry over from the real thing, and the thrusters are visible at the rear.
Thus, this is a simply CGI take on the model that imagines it in a different color, and to be honest it does not look bad at all. However, we will probably have to wait two more years before we will see it dressed in a similar color, because it is bound to hit the assembly line in 2028. That’s what Elon Musk claimed, anyway, and given that we know how Tesla rolls, we wouldn’t hold our breath for it. Not in 2028, anyway.
Photo: Instagram | theottle In case you forgot, the new Tesla Roadster was supposed to hit the assembly line back in 2020. That was six years ago. Clearly, the deadline was missed, and after that, Musk promised that the electric hypercar will hit the road in 2021, in 2022, and in 2023. And in 2023, it said that it will “hopefully” hit production in 2024. That didn’t happen either, and now we are in 2026, and the model is still not ready to arrive at dealers.
Far from it, actually, because the vehicle that you have seen in the official photos and videos, and the countless clips shared on social media recently, is nothing more than a prototype. Still, it is one that looks quite cool, in the official demonstration, anyway, and it has been modified from the concept seen back in 2017, as it is now a lot more angular, and some say that it looks like a mix between the Tesla Cybertruck and a supercar from a few years ago. And that’s not exactly a bad thing, is it?
Tesla decided to call this model the Roadster, as you already know, just like the original model made between 2008 and 2012, which was reengineered Lotus Elise. And we suspected that it would be named that, though some outlets bet on different monikers, such as the CyberRoadster, or the Roadster 2.0, among others.
Photo: Instagram | theottle Now, the new Tesla Roadster has finally been demonstrated after further delays, proving that it is capable of pulling some jaw-dropping stunts, like jumping over various obstacles, and then breaking its fall. The automaker claims that it features fans underneath the provide 2Gs of downforce while the car stands still. On top of that, it also boasts no fewer than 10 cold-gas thrusters. These allow it to maneuver mid-air, and they are fed by a pair of 600-liter ultra-high-pressure air tanks that are on deck.
Elon Musk claimed that this is simply atmospheric air, so the tanks can be replenished on their own while the vehicle is being driven. These thrusters also turn the new Tesla Roadster into a veritable rocket, which takes a neck-snapping 0.81 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from rest. That’s what the company claims, anyway, though let’s not forget that this thing is still a prototype, and it will hit the road two years from now in the most realistic scenario, though we wouldn’t hold our breath for that debut date to be honest.
You see, despite the impressive demonstration that has taken the World Wide Web by storm, the Tesla Roadster hasn’t been detailed. Thus, we do not know how much power it has, what wheels are being driven (it’s probably all four, though) what the battery capacity is, how far it can travel, what is the production capacity, where it will be made, where it will launch initially, and other such details.
The official website reveals that the new Tesla Roadster will be offered in three trim levels. These will be called the Performance, Thrust, and Rocket, and it’s the mid-spec that can supposedly hit 60 mph in less than one second, and this one costs $250,000. The model that can fly is an “Invite Only,” and it is a single-seat version, by the looks of it. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Theo throttle – the fudger (@theottle)
